title: Controlled Metamorphosis: Ring Size, Resistance Cost and Saved Passive Points in 0.5
summary: Controlled Metamorphosis is a Unique Diamond Jewel in Path of Exile 2 0.5.4 that creates a ring-shaped (annulus) radius for remote passive allocation and applies -(20-5)% to all Elemental Resistances. This guide covers the eight ring sizes, why it is not a normal circular radius, how the Elemental Resistance penalty is calculated, the removal of the old Chaos Resistance penalty in 0.4.0, Divine Orb rerolls, the Cost-Benefit table, and how it differs from From Nothing.
description: How Controlled Metamorphosis works in PoE2 0.5.4: a Unique Diamond with a variable ring radius for remote allocation, the Elemental Resistance cost, the Xesht +4 drop, and build planning.

sections.title: Quick answer
sections.callout: Controlled Metamorphosis is a Unique Diamond Jewel that forms two rings (an annulus) around its socket. Passives that fall inside the ring band can be allocated without being connected, but nodes in the inner circle do nothing. It applies -(20-5)% to all Elemental Resistances (the old Chaos Resistance penalty was removed in 0.4.0). It is always Corrupted, cannot be chanced, and drops only from Xesht, We That Are One at +4 Breach.
calloutDetail: The ring size rolls 1-8 (Very Small to Massive) and is independent of the resistance penalty - a Massive ring with -5% Elemental is the best copy.
You still pay the passive point for every node you allocate; the jewel only removes the pathing requirement.

answers.label: Avoid

sections.title: Overview, ring-size visual and current versus legacy
paragraphs: Controlled Metamorphosis is the only Unique Jewel whose allocation zone is a ring (an annulus) rather than a filled circle. When socketed into an allocated Jewel Socket, it draws two concentric rings: an inner ring and an outer ring. Any passive node that falls on the band between those two rings - the annulus - can be allocated without being connected to your tree. Crucially, the space inside the inner ring is dead: nodes there cannot be taken through the jewel, which is the single biggest surprise for new users who expect a normal circular radius.

Picture the passive tree as a grid of nodes. Place the Jewel Socket at the centre. Draw a small circle of radius r1 (the inner ring) and a larger circle of radius r2 (the outer ring) around it. The annulus is the donut-shaped band between r1 and r2. Nodes sitting on that donut are reachable; nodes strictly inside r1 and nodes outside r2 are not. Because the band is thin, the ring size roll (1-8) decides how many useful nodes land on it - which is why a bigger ring is not automatically better: it depends on whether your target nodes actually sit on the band at that size.

The jewel also applies -(20-5)% to all Elemental Resistances. This penalty is independent of the ring size: every copy, from Very Small to Massive, can roll anywhere in that range, and a Massive ring with a -5% roll is the most valuable combination. You still pay the passive point for every node you allocate; the jewel only removes the pathing requirement, so the saving is the pathing points you skip.

Current versus legacy: before patch 0.4.0, Controlled Metamorphosis also applied -(23-3)% to Chaos Resistance. That Chaos line was removed in 0.4.0 and does not return on new 0.5.4 drops - only the Elemental penalty remains. Legacy copies dropped before 0.4.0 keep their Chaos penalty. There is also a documented edge case where a corrupted roll of 9 or higher (outside the 1-8 range) makes the ring-size modifier disappear and the jewel forms no ring; treat any such copy as a bug-affected outlier and trade only for valid 1-8 rolls.
bullets: Allocation zone is an annulus (two rings), not a filled disc.
Inner circle is dead space; only the ring band allocates.
Ring size rolls 1-8 (Very Small to Massive), independent of resistance.
Resistance penalty: -(20-5)% all Elemental; no Chaos line in 0.5.4.
You still pay the point for every node; only pathing is skipped.
Legacy pre-0.4.0 copies kept a Chaos Resistance penalty; new drops do not.

sections.title: Eligibility: what the ring can reach
note: Only the annulus - the band between the inner and outer ring - allocates nodes. The inner circle and everything beyond the outer ring are excluded.

values.text: Both rings of the annulus allocate nodes; this is the only zone that works.
Unlike a normal circular radius, the space between the two rings does nothing.
Beyond the outer ring you must path normally.
The socket must already be allocated on the tree before the ring forms.
Every copy lowers all Elemental Resistances; gear must compensate.

steps.label: Reach an allocated Jewel Socket
body: Socket the jewel in any allocated Jewel Socket; the socket must already be allocated before the ring forms.

steps.label: Read the rolled ring size
body: The jewel rolls a ring size 1-8 (Very Small to Massive) and an Elemental Resistance penalty -(20-5)%. Both are fixed by the drop/corruption.

steps.label: Allocate the ring band
body: Nodes that fall inside the two rings (the annulus) can be allocated without connection. The inner circle is dead space.

steps.label: Compensate resistances
body: Recover the lost Elemental Resistances on gear suffixes; Chaos Inoculation builds ignore the penalty entirely.

steps.label: Divine to improve (optional)
body: A Divine Orb rerolls the Elemental Resistance penalty toward -5% and can reroll the ring size within 1-8.

before: Pathing to a perimeter cluster around a central socket costs every intermediate node between your tree and that band.
after: Those same perimeter nodes are allocated directly from the ring band, skipping the connecting path.
compare.note: The jewel trades one Jewel Socket plus Elemental Resistance suffixes for the pathing points you skip on the ring band.

intro: Controlled Metamorphosis pays off when a build's useful nodes form a perimeter around a socket it can already reach. The four personas below show where it shines.

sections.title: Alternatives
paragraphs: A normal or Rare Diamond Jewel gives flat stats for the same socket with no resistance cost and no ring-size gamble. If your target nodes are cheap to path to, a Rare jewel is usually the safer value.

From Nothing is the closest cousin: it also remote-allocates, but through a fixed disc around a bound Keystone and with no resistance penalty - at the cost of being Keystone-locked. Megalomaniac grants random Notables directly. Against the Darkness boosts small passives in a radius. Pick by what your tree actually needs.

Because Controlled Metamorphosis costs Elemental Resistance suffixes, the real alternative is often just pathing normally and using the socket for a Rare jewel or a resistance-friendly unique - only commit when the skipped pathing clearly beats the suffix loss.
bullets: Rare Diamond Jewel: flexible stats, no resistance cost.
From Nothing: fixed disc remote allocation, no resistance cost, Keystone-locked.
Normal pathing: often cheaper than a wrong-ring-size copy.

entries.question: Why can't I allocate a node that looks inside the radius?
summary: A player expected a filled circular radius and could not take a node in the centre.
editorialAnalysis: Controlled Metamorphosis forms an annulus, not a disc. Only the band between the inner and outer ring allocates; the inner circle is dead space. A node that looks 'inside' may sit in that dead centre.
officialAnswer: Only the ring band (between the two rings) allocates nodes; the inner circle does not.

entries.question: Does it still have a Chaos Resistance penalty?
summary: A guide noted the old -(23-3)% Chaos Resistance and asked whether it remains.
editorialAnalysis: Patch 0.4.0 removed the Chaos Resistance line. Current 0.5.4 drops have only -(20-5)% to all Elemental Resistances. Pre-0.4.0 legacy copies keep their Chaos penalty; new drops do not.
officialAnswer: Current 0.5.4 has no Chaos Resistance penalty; only the Elemental penalty remains.

entries.question: What does a corrupted roll above 8 do to the ring?
summary: Database notes record that a ring value of 9 or higher makes the ring-size modifier disappear.
editorialAnalysis: The ring size rolls 1-8. A corrupted value of 9+ is outside the valid range and the jewel forms no ring (documented as likely a bug). Trade only for valid 1-8 rolls; such outliers should be treated as bug-affected.
officialAnswer: Valid ring sizes are 1-8; values outside that range drop the ring modifier and the jewel allocates nothing.

entries.question: Is a bigger ring always better?
summary: A video explained that ring size value depends on where your useful nodes sit.
editorialAnalysis: Because only the band allocates, a Massive ring helps only if your target nodes land on its band. A smaller ring can be better when the nodes you want sit closer to the socket. Trade value still favours larger rings.
officialAnswer: Larger is not automatically better; match the ring size to your target nodes, though trade prices rise with size.

problems.symptom: Node is visually near the socket but cannot be allocated
directAnswer: Current normal rule: only the two rings (the annulus) allocate nodes; the inner circle between them does nothing. Historical bug: very early versions sometimes allocated the inner circle inconsistently. Current reproducible: no - the inner circle is dead by design; place the socket so target nodes fall on the ring band.
checks: Check whether the node sits inside the inner circle; if so, move the socket or pick a different ring size.

problems.symptom: I allocated a node but the character sheet did not change
directAnswer: Current normal rule: you still pay a passive point for every allocated node; the jewel only removes pathing, not the node cost. Historical bug: a past display lag showed stale sheet values. Current reproducible: no for the rule; if the sheet is stale, re-open the tree. Confirm the node is genuinely inside the ring band.
checks: Verify the node is inside the ring band and the jewel is socketed; re-open the character sheet.

problems.symptom: Jewel will not remove / nodes stay allocated after removal
directAnswer: Current normal rule: removing the jewel unallocates all ring nodes and refunds their points. Historical bug: an older client sometimes left nodes visually allocated until re-login. Current reproducible: no - removal correctly refunds; if nodes persist, re-log and re-check.
checks: Right-click to remove; if nodes remain, re-log and confirm refund.

problems.symptom: Jewel dropped with no Chaos Resistance penalty
directAnswer: Current normal rule: 0.5.4 Controlled Metamorphosis has only -(20-5)% to all Elemental Resistances; the old -(23-3)% Chaos Resistance was removed in 0.4.0 and does not return on new drops. Historical: pre-0.4.0 copies did have Chaos penalty. Current reproducible: a new drop never has Chaos penalty.
checks: Read the tooltip; if you see a Chaos penalty it is a legacy 0.4.0-or-earlier copy.
